newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian cash would spark hyperinflation - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: New Russian cash would spark hyperinflation - c.bank.

text.p: Doubling Russian money supply, as proposed by Communist deputies, would trigger hyperinflation with prices rising tens of thousands of percent a year, the head of Russia's central bank was quoted as saying on Wednesday.

"When I saw the bill on new cash, my first thought was that an enemy country's agents had decided to finish off Russia's economy and suggested this plan," Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin told Interfax news agency.

Communist deputies in the State Duma lower house of parliament have proposed printing another 330 trillion roubles to help Russia overcome its budget crisis. The Communist move is an alternative to government proposals for spending cuts of 108 trillion roubles.

Russia's cash in circulation is currently about 300 trillion roubles, said Dubinin, who has presided over a sharp fall in the annual inflation rate to about 15 percent currently from 161 percent when he was appointed in November 1995.

"It is hard for me to imagine the consequences of such an injection of cash into the economy. It would be a surreal picture," Dubinin said. "We have never looked into an option of doubling monetary supply, even theoretically," he said.

Central bank experts had calculated that a 35-40 rise in money supply percent would lead to 30 percent monthly inflation, similar to that of 1992-1993, after Russia freed prices in its tough drive towards market economy. The monthly rate is now about 1.0 percent.
The Duma will discuss the bill, together with the government plan to cut spending, at its session on May 21.
Communist deputies say money supply makes up only 12 percent of Russia's gross domestic product, a much lower proportion than in Western countries.
